name_reason: Conforms to fd2_<domain>_<descriptor>. domain=chapter_event_handler; descriptor encodes the meaningful domain IDs: 3c = dispatch index 0x3C (table entry @0x51C81; (0x51C81-0x51B91)/4 = 0x3C, verified), ch26 = chapter 26 (valid 01-30 ID), ai_ctrl = semantic (disarms an AI control flag). No Ghidra address residue: own address is 0x35675, unrelated to '3c'. Sibling handlers (3b/3d/...) follow the same dispatch-index naming.
purpose: Chapter-26 tile-step event handler (dispatch idx 0x3C): when a non-enemy steps the trigger tile, disarm the AI control flag for two NPC char ranges.
logic_summary: Reads runtime_char_array[stepping_char_id].team (combat-record team byte). If team != 0 (stepper is NPC/player, not an enemy with team==0), calls fd2_set_combat_aux_block_byte_d_low4_for_char_range twice -- (0x17,0x18,0) for chars 0x17..0x18 and (0x35,0x38,0) for chars 0x35..0x38 -- writing 0 into the low nibble of each char's pCombat_aux_block[0xD] (the per-event AI/dialog control flag). Total 2+4 = 6 chars disarmed. No dialog. Function has a __CHK(0x10) stack-frame check prologue. In the binary the 2nd call + ADD ESP,0xC + RET is a Class-3 shared tail at 0x356AE borrowed (unconditional JMP from 0x35F6A) by fd2_chapter_event_handler_50__ch30_ai_ctrl; that is a code-sharing size optimisation, functionally two complete calls.

params.name: stepping_char_id
params.semantics: Tile-step ABI arg (read at [ESP+0x4] after the __CHK PUSH 0x10): the char id that stepped onto the trigger tile. Used only to index runtime_char_array[].team for the enemy/non-enemy gate.
params.reason: Accurate and descriptive; matches the tile-step ABI usage. No address residue.

returns.semantics: No return value (handler invoked via per-event dispatch table @ 0x51B91).

notes: Source comment block (chevt2.c lines 580-599) is already accurate and consistent with the Ghidra plate (no contradiction): both describe the team!=0 gate, the two char ranges 0x17..0x18 and 0x35..0x38, the AI-control-flag-disarm semantics, and the Class-3 shared tail @0x356AE consumed by handler_50. No Edit to src and no plate change required. Writes to pCombat_aux_block[0xD] happen inside the callee, not in this function, so writes_globals is empty here. Note (not an issue): decompiler labels the team field .bTeam; src uses the field name .team via the runtime-char struct -- semantically identical, the field byte at runtime_char offset +6.
